newsitem.title: USA: AOL on target for 10 mln clients--Chairman.
newsitem.headline: AOL on target for 10 mln clients--Chairman.

text.p: America Online Inc is on target to reach 10 million subscribers by the end of the calendar year, Chairman Steve Case said Thursday.
AOL added 600,000 net new members in the fourth quarter, which Case said is above the company's internal projections.
"We're on target to hit 10 million members by the end of the calendar year," Case told Reuters in an interview after the company released fourth quarter results.
The company reported earnings of $0.09 a share, excluding certain timing adjustments, which was above Wall Street analysts' estimates of around $0.07 a share.
The company reported a loss of $0.12 a share including adjustments AOL agreed to make after shifting from metered to flat-rate pricing and ending certain information provider agreements.
Case declined to say whether the company will be making any future adjustments.
Fourth quarter revenues were $475.7 million. Of these, Case said, advertising revenues tripled over the past year, and commerce revenues grew fourfold.
"We expect that to continue," he said.
The strong results pleased some. AOL shares closed Thursday at 71, but traders said AOL shares rose slightly in after-hours trading to 71-3/8, following release of its fourth quarter results.

"I think a lot of people on the Street will have to be pushing numbers up. Given the margin improvement you're seeing, there's probably a lot more room to the upside in the numbers than we're seeing," said Brian Oakes, a vice president at Lehman Bros.
He said AOL's gross margins on the quarter were over 40 percent, up over 400 basis points from the prior quarter.
He also noted the company's strong growth in domestic subscribers and improved gross margins.
Oakes said he expects future commerce and advertising announcements from the company after listening to a conference call on fourth quarter results.
